meta.description: Left-align and trim indels to parsimonious canonical form, decompose MNPs (atomize), and split multiallelic variants with bcftools norm. Use when comparing variants across callers or cohorts, preparing a VCF for database annotation or ClinVar/dbSNP matching, merging VCFs, reconciling vt-vs-bcftools representation discordance, or resolving the VCF-left-align vs HGVS-3'-rule clash.
meta.execution_note: Re-audit of the fixed Skill (fork commit c1237cdb). Mode A. Windows bcftools 1.24 (MSYS2); WSL agents distro: bcftools 1.21, vt, cyvcf2 0.34.0. Data SYNTHETIC (data/make_data.py, seed 20260911; edge_multiallelic*.vcf hand-written; runs/in7/mixed.vcf written for input 7). Only in4/in5 pre-fix scripts were kept, so inputs 1-4 were rebuilt from the pre-fix viewer with the post-fix commands (runs/p_in1..p_in5); inputs 6 and 7 are new (runs/in6, runs/in7). Phase-mode semantics checked against 'bcftools csq' help on 1.24 and 1.21. n_inputs 7 = 5 regression + 2 new. Inputs executed: 7/7.

scientific_integrity.detail: No fabricated values; Tan 2015 is the correct reference for the normal form.

practice_boundaries.detail: Representation and matching only; ClinVar assertions reported as leads with review status.

methodological_ground.detail: Order of operations, reference matching and the decompose-vs-annotate tension verified on data.

code_usability.detail: All bcftools, vt and cyvcf2 code and the shipped example ran; failures on the REF-mismatch file are the documented -c e behaviour.

functional_suitability.note: Split -> atomize -> left-align now emits no spurious ALT=* records (callerA, callerB, edge file); the single-pass -m-any --atomize claim, the -m-both/-m+both table and --old-rec-tag were verified. One error introduced by the fix: the csq caveat says -p m merges only where phase is known and -p s treats unphased hets as separate haplotypes; bcftools 1.21/1.24 help and runs show m merges all GTs and s skips unphased hets.

reliability.note: Example REF pre-check stops with a clear count and inspection command; Common Errors gained the atomize-order and unphased-het rows. The 'Before Database Annotation' block still writes a non-BGZF empty file on a REF mismatch and the index error that follows is misleading.

performance_context.note: 298-line SKILL.md; usage guide partly duplicates it.

agent_usability.note: Clear ordering rule with its reason; the wrong -p m/-p s wording is the one misleading sentence.

maintainability.note: Example no longer hides stderr and runs; no test data ships.

agent_specific.note: Precise trigger and hand-offs to annotation and clinical-interpretation.

key_strengths: Normal-form definition and the silent-miss mechanism are exact and were demonstrated (homopolymer deletion found in ClinVar only after normalization)
The pre-fix P1 is fixed and verified: splitting before atomizing removes the spurious ALT=* records, and the single-pass form was confirmed equivalent
The example now stops with a clear REF-mismatch message and reports zero atomization artifacts on MNP-free input

recommendations.title: csq --phase m and s described wrongly
recommendations.problem: The caveat says -p m merges only where phase is known and -p s treats unphased hets as separate haplotypes; bcftools 1.21/1.24 help: m merges all GTs into a single haplotype, s skips unphased hets (no consequence emitted in the run).
recommendations.root_cause: Mode semantics were paraphrased, not copied from 'bcftools csq' help.
recommendations.fix: Replace with the help text (a = GTs as is, 0/1 -> 0|1; m = merge all GTs; r = require phase; s = skip unphased hets) and recommend -p a for phased input.

recommendations.title: Database-annotation block leaves an empty file on REF error
recommendations.problem: On a REF mismatch the last pipe step aborts after creating a 0-record non-BGZF file; the next 'bcftools index' fails with 'not BGZF compressed', hiding the real cause.
recommendations.root_cause: The workflow blocks omit the REF pre-check the example now has.
recommendations.fix: Add `set -o pipefail` and a `bcftools norm -f ref.fa -c w` pre-check (or the example's MISMATCH count) before the pipeline.
